stories.title: Sacramento-area school district promotes AI literacy in the classroom
stories.simple_summary: A school district in Sacramento is teaching students about AI and how it works. This helps young people understand a technology that's becoming more common in everyday life.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have grandchildren in school, they're learning skills they'll need for jobs in the future. It's good that schools are teaching this early.

stories.title: Mark Zuckerberg has an Instagzam
stories.simple_summary: Instagram changed the look of its logo and brand name design. The new version looks quite different from what people are used to.
stories.why_it_matters: This doesn't affect how Instagram works or costs for users — it's just a visual change that Instagram decided to make.

stories.title: You can now turn off Google Gemini’s visible watermarks
stories.simple_summary: Google is letting people remove the watermark (a small sparkly mark) that appears on images and videos made by its AI tools. Think of it like removing a company stamp from a document.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use Google's AI to create images, you now have the choice to hide that watermark — though Google keeps an invisible marker to track where the image came from.

stories.title: Google will now allow users to remove visible watermark from its AI generations
stories.simple_summary: Google will keep an invisible watermark on AI-made files even if you hide the visible one. This invisible mark helps identify that the file was made by AI.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to tech professionals and people worried about AI-made content fraud — nothing most small business owners need to act on.

stories.title: The unexpected issue dividing parties and midterms candidates
stories.simple_summary: This headline is too vague to explain without more details about what the issue actually is.
stories.why_it_matters: Without knowing what the issue is, I can't tell you if it matters.

stories.title: Does Mark Zuckerberg really believe AI is ‘for everyone’?
stories.simple_summary: Mark Zuckerberg released a simple AI tool that anyone can download and use on their own computer, saying AI should be available to everyone instead of locked up by big companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually mean more small businesses can use AI tools without paying big companies, but right now it's more of a technical announcement for people comfortable installing software.

stories.title: Kog is going deeper to squeeze more inference out of GPUs
stories.simple_summary: A startup says that special computer chips (GPUs) might actually be better suited for certain AI tasks than people thought.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a technical story for investors and engineers — nothing that affects your daily life or small business.

stories.title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
stories.simple_summary: Amazon and Google are making big profits from AI, which shows that AI technology is making money for large companies.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to stock investors — it doesn't directly affect customers or small business owners.

stories.title: Hyperscalers might regret embracing natural gas if new forecast proves correct
stories.simple_summary: Natural gas prices could get much more expensive in some areas, and that would make it very costly for big tech companies to run their AI data centers (the huge computer warehouses that power AI).
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a small business, this probably won't affect you directly — it's mainly a problem for massive tech companies.

stories.title: Meta’s ‘open’ AI, and a $250M deal gone very wrong
stories.simple_summary: Mark Zuckerberg released a basic AI tool anyone can use, saying AI should be open to everyone. There's also mention of a $250 million deal that went wrong, but details aren't given.
stories.why_it_matters: In the future, this could make AI tools more affordable and available for small business owners, but it's too early to know if it will actually happen that way.

stories.title: Not Micron, Not Sandisk. This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Could Be the Next Nvidia.
stories.simple_summary: Someone is predicting that a certain company's AI memory chip stock could become very valuable, like Nvidia stock did.
stories.why_it_matters: This is investment advice and speculation — it has nothing to do with running a small business or everyday life.

stories.title: Apple trained its own AI model for China with help from Alibaba
stories.simple_summary: Apple created a special AI system for use in China by working together with a Chinese company called Alibaba. This is unusual because of tensions between the U.S. and China.
stories.why_it_matters: If you sell products or services in China, this might mean Apple will have better AI tools there — but for most small business owners, this is just news about big companies.
